seo.title: H300 4G & H500 NB-IoT Asset Tracking | Hitelecom
seo.description: Find equipment, manage reusable assets and follow cargo with H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT tracking. Select positioning and reporting to suit your deployment.

hero.description: The Hitelecom H300 (4G) and H500 (NB-IoT) asset tracking sensors help teams locate equipment, reusable packaging and cargo between sites. Use location reports to plan collection, return and the next deployment. Choose the model around coverage and reporting needs, then match the positioning method, power, mounting and platform connection to the asset.

features.title: Find the asset you need
features.text: Use location information to find the equipment, carrier or case needed for the next job. Positioning detail is specified for the asset and its working area.

features.title: H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT
features.text: Two radio models for different deployments. Choose using operator support at your sites and route stages, together with the reporting schedule you need.

features.title: Reports that prompt an action
features.text: Geofence or movement events can be specified where an alert helps the team arrange collection, check a site transfer or follow up a deployment.

features.title: Keep location with the asset record
features.text: Connect equipment or carrier identity to location reports. Add the platform maps, timestamps and history needed for collection and return planning to the project scope.

features.title: Fit the working environment
features.text: Select the enclosure around dust, rain, cleaning and handling exposure. The supplied specification identifies its protection rating and installation conditions.

features.title: Power for the job cycle
features.text: Stored equipment and assets in transit need different update schedules. Match the power arrangement to that schedule, maintenance access and the target service interval.

features.title: A consistent fleet rollout
features.text: Plan activation and device-to-asset identification so installers connect each tracker to the correct unit. Local setup options, including NFC, are specified where required.

features.title: Mount it to the right carrier
features.text: Use an equipment frame, a protected recess or a transport-case bracket. Choose attachment hardware with room for normal handling, access and reception.

positioning.description: The useful position depends on the job: an outdoor yard, a customer site or a particular indoor zone. GPS or BeiDou, cellular location and local indoor systems are project options; select the approach around the required detail and the places the asset moves.

cards.title: Outdoor equipment and cargo
cards.text: For outdoor yards and transport stages, consider a satellite-positioning design using GPS or BeiDou where included. A protected mounting point still needs suitable antenna exposure, especially around metal equipment or shipping cases.
cards.project_brief: Location objective · Positioning design · Antenna exposure · Reporting frequency

cards.title: Approximate site location
cards.text: Cellular LBS, where included, can support an approximate site-level position. Its usefulness depends on the available operator service and the detail the team needs, so check it at the actual holding sites.
cards.project_brief: Operator support · Location service · Site-level objective · Pilot validation

cards.title: Indoor equipment finding
cards.text: A building zone, aisle or equipment bay needs a project-specific indoor design. BLE, Wi-Fi or another local arrangement is reviewed with its infrastructure and integration, rather than inferred from the cellular radio model.
cards.project_brief: Building layout · Required location detail · Local infrastructure · Integration

positioning.installation_text: Choose a protected frame, recess or carrier bracket that leaves normal handling and service access clear. Check attachment retention and reception on the actual asset, then confirm that reports reach the intended platform at representative sites and route stages.

workflow.profile_text: A trailer at a customer yard needs a collection plan. A test instrument needs to reach calibration. A crate pool needs to come back before the next season. Give each tracked asset an identity and an update schedule that helps the responsible team do that job.

steps.title: Locate
steps.text: Connect the tracker to the equipment, case or carrier ID so the team can find the correct asset.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Send the required location reports through the selected H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT service. Set the update schedule around storage, transfer and collection.

steps.title: Respond
steps.text: Use the location information to arrange pickup, assign a transfer or return the asset to its pool. Platform history and alerts are included where specified.

workflow.battery_text: More frequent positioning and reports generally use more energy. Set an update schedule that serves the job, then assess the power arrangement against operating temperatures, network service and maintenance access. The selected model’s supplied specification sets the basis for the service-interval estimate.
workflow.platform_text: Bring location reports into the asset records your team already uses. A Hitelecom Cloud or customer-platform connection can be reviewed for the project, including asset IDs, data fields and access. MQTT is considered where included in the integration design.

applicationSection.title: Asset visibility.
applicationSection.description: Find practical tracking jobs for equipment, reusable assets and cargo. Each task shows what the team needs to find or collect, where a tracker could fit and which deployment details matter for the proposal.
applicationSection.note: AI-generated application illustrations show representative asset environments.
applicationSection.mountingNote: Candidate mounting points must leave handling and service access clear. Confirm the attachment with the asset owner and check retention and reception on the actual unit.

faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for model selection, mounting, location detail, reporting and the data connection your team needs.

faqs.question: How do we choose between H300 4G and H500 NB-IoT?
paragraphs: H300 uses 4G; H500 uses NB-IoT. Choose between them using the operator service available at your deployment sites and route stages, then review modem bands, SIM arrangements, roaming and the required update schedule. For moving or cross-border assets, validate service across the route. Positioning, power and platform functions are agreed for the selected configuration.

faqs.question: How should we plan tracking inside warehouses or covered sites?
paragraphs: Indoor finding needs a design matched to the required detail: a building, zone, aisle or equipment bay. Buildings, metalwork and covered storage affect reception. For finer indoor positions, a project-specific BLE, Wi-Fi or other local system needs supporting infrastructure and integration. Check that design against the actual mounting point and the locations where the team needs to find the asset.

faqs.question: How do reporting intervals affect battery life?
paragraphs: More frequent positioning and reports generally use more energy. Choose the update schedule that helps the team collect, transfer or return the asset, then assess power against network service, operating conditions and maintenance access. The battery-life or service-interval estimate should state the selected configuration and the reporting profile it is based on.

faqs.question: How should we specify geofence and movement alerts?
paragraphs: Request geofence and movement alerts when they will help the team act on a site transfer or deployment. The supplied tracker and platform scope must include the required events. Specify the boundary, update schedule, timing, recipients and follow-up action, then check that the resulting notification meets the job’s needs under the site’s coverage conditions.

faqs.question: How is the tracker attached to equipment or packaging?
paragraphs: Use attachment hardware that fits the asset: a frame bracket, protected recess or case pocket may be appropriate, with magnet, screw or strap arrangements considered for the project. Keep lifting paths, stacking faces, closures and service access clear. Check retention and reception on the actual unit, and specify the cleaning, temperature or chemical exposure the enclosure must accommodate.

faqs.question: How should we plan cross-border and sea routes?
paragraphs: Check operator service for the selected radio in every country and route stage, including modem bands, SIM arrangements and roaming. H300 uses 4G; H500 uses NB-IoT. Port and inland reporting depends on terrestrial service. For offshore stages, any additional connectivity or recording system needs a separate confirmed design and specification before it is included in the proposal.

faqs.question: Can location reports connect to our own platform?
paragraphs: A connection to your own platform is a project option. Share the asset records and location fields the team needs, together with the endpoint, access and notification requirements. MQTT can form part of the agreed integration where included. A sample message and a complete data-path check establish how reports will appear in your dispatch, asset-management or transport workflow.

faqs.question: Can the product design and additional sensing be customized?
paragraphs: Yes. Hitelecom offers OEM/ODM review around the asset and its deployment. Photos or drawings help establish available space, attachment, handling, power and connectivity needs. Additional temperature, humidity, tilt or light-based opening measurements can be scoped where useful; the proposal identifies the included channels, performance and platform connection for the supplied configuration.
